turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Hi Sam, it's Priya from Northstar. Is now still a good time for a quick call?

turns.speaker: Sam
turns.text: Sure, I have a couple of minutes before my next meeting.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Great. I work with operations teams that are trying to keep orders moving without adding headcount. I wanted to understand how your team handles that today.

turns.speaker: Sam
turns.text: We use a spreadsheet and a lot of manual checks. It's getting messy as we grow.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: That's really common. How much time does the team lose to those manual checks each week?

turns.speaker: Sam
turns.text: Probably five hours a week, maybe more when orders pile up.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: That's a lot. We can definitely cut that in half, and most teams see the difference in the first month.

turns.speaker: Sam
turns.text: I'm not sure we have budget this quarter.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: That's fair. Would it help if I sent a short summary you could share with your manager?

turns.speaker: Sam
turns.text: Maybe. Send me something I can share with my manager.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Absolutely. I'll send a one-page summary today. Can we book 20 minutes on Thursday to walk through it together?

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Perfect. I'll send an invite and the summary this afternoon. Thanks, Sam.

turns.speaker: Sam
turns.text: Actually, before we finish, what does implementation involve? I need to know what my team is signing up for.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Good question. It usually takes a couple of weeks, depending on how we connect to your systems. I can cover that on Thursday.

missed_moments.what_happened: Sam named the time cost, and Priya moved straight into a product claim instead of asking what that time was worth.
missed_moments.why_it_hurt: Without a business cost, the budget conversation had nothing concrete to justify.
missed_moments.better_alternative: What does five hours a week cost you in missed orders or overtime?

playbook_refs.chapter: Discovery that earns the next call
playbook_refs.excerpt: Ask what the problem costs before you describe what your product does. The cost is what makes the next conversation urgent.
